title: Symmetry and lines of symmetry
canonical_examples_source: Arithmetic self-verified; method ref: NCERT Class 5/6 Maths; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024 maths.

blocks.content: A shape has symmetry when you can fold it so both halves match exactly. The fold line is called a line of symmetry. Quick words: mirror images means two halves that look like reflections in a mirror. fold line means the crease made when you fold paper in half.
A line of symmetry divides a shape into two halves that are mirror images of each other.

steps: Fold a square top to bottom — the halves match.
Fold it side to side, and along both diagonals — all match.
So a square has 4 lines of symmetry.

blocks.prompt: A square has ___ lines of symmetry.
blocks.explain: A square can be folded to match along 4 different lines.
blocks.rule: A line of symmetry splits a shape into two mirror-image halves.

blocks.content: Some shapes have many lines of symmetry, and some have none at all.

blocks.question: Which shape has MORE lines of symmetry?
blocks.explain: A square has 4 lines of symmetry; a rectangle has only 2.
blocks.rule: The number of lines of symmetry depends on the shape; a square has more than a rectangle.

practiceItems.prompt: does a circle have many lines of symmetry? (yes/no)
lines of symmetry in a rectangle

lines of symmetry in a square

blocks.question: Mia folds a square in half two ways (top-to-bottom and side-to-side) and says it has 2 lines of symmetry. Has she found them all?
options: No — a square has 4 lines of symmetry (2 straight and 2 diagonal)
blocks.explain: The two folds Mia found are real lines of symmetry, but she missed the diagonals. Fold a square corner-to-corner and the halves still match. That gives 2 more, so 4 lines in total.
blocks.rule: Check every possible fold, including the diagonals.
blocks.principle: A shape can have lines of symmetry you miss if you only try the obvious folds.
canonical_solution: A square has 4 lines of symmetry

rubric.look_for: tries diagonal folds as well as straight ones
explains checking all folds, including diagonals

misconceptions.coach: Try the diagonals too — a square folds corner to corner.

misconceptions.if: counts diagonals of a rectangle the same way
misconceptions.coach: A non-square rectangle has only 2 lines; the square is special.

blocks.content: If a fold makes two matching halves, that fold is a line of symmetry. Some shapes have several. Let's practise!
